splits.issue: Whether an Appeal or Revision filed ON or AFTER 1 July 2024 against a conviction/order passed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by CrPC 1973 or BNSS 2023 under Section 531(2)(a).

Kerala_High_Court.held: Appeals filed on or after 01.07.2024 must be instituted under BNSS 2023.
Kerala_High_Court.reasoning: Section 531(2)(a) saves only those appeals that were actually 'pending' immediately before 01.07.2024. If an appeal was not yet filed before 01.07.2024, it was not pending, so the new procedure under BNSS applies.

Punjab_and_Haryana_High_Court.case_citation: Mandeep Singh v. State of Punjab & Anr., CRM-M-34128-2024
Punjab_and_Haryana_High_Court.held: Appeals arising out of pre-July 2024 judgments continue under CrPC 1973.
Punjab_and_Haryana_High_Court.reasoning: Right of appeal is a substantive vested right that crystallizes on the date of institution of original lis/trial. Section 531(2)(a) must be interpreted constructively to preserve the continuous chain of CrPC proceedings.

Delhi_High_Court.case_citation: Prince v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2024 DHC 5291
Delhi_High_Court.held: Differentiated strictly between pending trials vs new petitions instituted after 01.07.2024; procedural applications filed post 01.07.2024 must cite BNSS provisions.
Delhi_High_Court.reasoning: Literal rule of interpretation applies to Sec 531(2)(a).

Bombay_High_Court.case_citation: XX v. State of Maharashtra, 2024 BHC
Bombay_High_Court.held: If trial/investigation was already underway under CrPC, the statutory right of appeal is an extension of that trial and retains CrPC character.
Bombay_High_Court.reasoning: Doctrine of vested procedural rights as enunciated in Garikapati Veeraya v. Subbiah Choudhry.

splits.advisory: High Courts are split on this question. In Kerala and Delhi, invoke BNSS provisions (Section 415/417 BNSS). In Punjab & Haryana and Bombay, invoke CrPC provisions (Section 374/378 CrPC). Always mention both in pleadings with a non-prejudice clause.

splits.issue: Whether an application for Anticipatory Bail or Regular Bail filed on or after 01.07.2024 for an offence/FIR registered before 01.07.2024 should be filed under Section 438/439 CrPC or Section 482/483 BNSS.

Punjab_and_Haryana_High_Court.case_citation: XX v. State of UT Chandigarh, 2024 PHHC
Punjab_and_Haryana_High_Court.held: If the bail application itself is filed on or after 01.07.2024, it must be under Section 482/483 BNSS, but if the FIR was registered prior to 01.07.2024, the investigation remains under CrPC.
Punjab_and_Haryana_High_Court.governing_statute: BNSS_2023 (for petition label) / CrPC_1973 (for investigation scope)

Rajasthan_High_Court.case_citation: Krishna Joshi v. State of Rajasthan, 2024 Raj HC
Rajasthan_High_Court.held: Applications filed after 01.07.2024 will be governed by BNSS 2023 provisions.

Bombay_High_Court.case_citation: Digambar v. State of Maharashtra, 2024 BHC
Bombay_High_Court.held: Applications under CrPC 438 are maintainable if investigation was initiated prior to 01.07.2024, and mere wrong captioning under CrPC/BNSS will not be a ground for rejection.

splits.advisory: State High Courts universally treat caption defects as curable, but procedural hearings will adhere to BNSS Section 482/483 if filed after July 1, 2024, while substantive penal evaluation remains strictly under IPC 1860.
